topic: CORRECTION: the partition change never improved the candidate; the apparent gain was vendor-side window variance

correction.retracted_claim: R54 reported that core-contiguous partitioning lifted gated prefill from 0.7574 to 0.8248 (+8.9%)
correction.why_retracted: the candidate median barely moved between those two runs (0.080056 -> 0.079435 ms, about 0.8%, i.e. noise), while the vendor median moved the other way (0.059085 -> 0.064479 ms, about +9%). The ratio difference is vendor variance, not a candidate improvement.
correction.conclusion: the candidate time is stable across all four gates (0.079-0.083 ms). The vendor time is not (0.055-0.065 ms, about +/-18%). A single window cannot characterise the ratio, and the best-looking window must not be quoted as the result.

implication.best_supported_statement: prefill runs about 0.079-0.083 ms while the vendor runs 0.055-0.065 ms, so the ratio is roughly 0.69-0.83 depending on the window, typically near 0.70-0.75
implication.gap: to reach parity the candidate must fall to at most the vendor time, so prefill needs roughly 20-30% less time
implication.what_is_not_proven: no partition or scheduling variant has been shown to change the candidate time at all; decode EXCEED 1.2809 stands on its own gated window
